caption: The drawing features two separate wooden objects displayed on a plain, light tan sheet. On the left side, there is a rectangular wooden comb with six widely spaced, long teeth, and the top part includes two circular holes. The comb has a natural brown coloration, with texture lines suggesting wood grain, and there are shadows indicating some depth and thickness. On the right side is a long, narrow object, which curves at the bottom end and appears to be a back scratcher. It is shaded to show a smooth, gradually curving surface and has a similar brown wooden color with visible grain patterns. Handwritten text near each object provides descriptive information, such as the object's name, the material (wooden), the date "Oct. 10th, '35", the Penobscot Tribe, and the object's size or function. The paper shows perforated holes along the top edge, suggesting it was taken from a sketchbook.
title: Comb and Back Scratcher
